props.name: methanol-forming catalyzer (generic)
props.description: the catalyzers most suitable for synthesizing oxygen-containing organic compounds from hydrogen and carbon monoxide, which also polymerize and hydrogenate the aromatic and nonsaturated hydrocarbons

evidence.note: continues 'taining oxygen, are at the same time those by means of which the aromatic hydrocarbons and the nonsaturated hydrocarbons can be polymerized (or condensed) and combined with hydrogen'

means of which the aromatic hydrocarbons and the nonsaturated hydrocarbons can be polymerized (or condensed) and combined with hydrogen in the most practical manner.

props.name: coal distillation gas can be used directly as additional hydrogen source

evidence.quote: The invention thus permits of directly 120 using coal distillation gas, after only tars and ammonia have been eliminated there- from, as an additional source of the hydro- gen to be added to water gas,

props.statement: The invention permits directly using coal distillation gas, after only tars and ammonia have been eliminated, as an additional source of hydrogen to be added to water gas for methanol synthesis gas mixtures.

props.name: the hydrocarbon layer is an excellent engine fuel

evidence.quote: This product when simply filtered, constitutes an excellent fuel for internal combustion engines

props.statement: The hydrocarbon upper layer of the 2nd example, simply filtered, constitutes an excellent fuel for internal combustion engines such as aeroplane or motor vehicle engines.

the armatic hydrocarbons which can be found in industrial gas mixtures such as coal distillation gas, or which are purposely

props.statement: Nonsaturated or aromatic hydrocarbons present in industrial gas mixtures such as coal distillation gas, or purposely added, are not prejudicial to the direct catalytic combination of carbon monoxide and hydrogen into methanol, and even seem to further it.

props.name: invention: methanol synthesis from a gas containing unsaturated or aromatic hydrocarbons

evidence.quote: This invention thus consists in using for synthesizing methyl alcohol by a catalytic & action under pressure upon a mixture of car- bon oxides and hydrogen, a gas mixture con- taining the latter components together with nonsaturated hydrocarbons
(ethylene, acety- len or homologous compounds) or aromatic 60 hydrocarbons (benzene, toluene . . .)

props.statement: The invention consists in using, for synthesizing methyl alcohol by catalytic action under pressure on carbon oxides and hydrogen, a gas mixture that also contains nonsaturated hydrocarbons (ethylene, acetylene or homologues) or aromatic hydrocarbons (benzene, toluene), coming from the source of the gas or purposely added.

props.name: the condensed product is slightly hydrated methanol with hydrocarbons in solution

evidence.quote: it consists of slightly hydrated me- thanol having hydrocarbons in solution; it may be employed without further treatment for heating purposes or for carburetion;

props.statement: The liquid condensed under pressure consists of slightly hydrated methanol with hydrocarbons in solution; it may be used without further treatment for heating or carburetion, or the hydrocarbons are separated by decantation after adding water and the methanol distilled.

props.name: operation continues until hydrogen is reduced to 4-5%

evidence.quote: the production of metha- nol is scarcely reduced, whilst the partial pressure of hydrogen in the gas mixture sub- jected to catalysis 1s hardly over 34 atm.
when operating at a total pressure of 800-1000 atm. the operation can be continued with a satisfactory output until the percent- age of hydrogen in the mixture is reduced to 4 or 5 per cent.

props.statement: Toward the end of the 1st example the methanol production is scarcely reduced while the hydrogen partial pressure is hardly over 34 atm, so at a total pressure of 800-1000 atm the operation can be continued with satisfactory output until the hydrogen in the mixture is reduced to 4 or 5 per cent.

props.name: more than 25% of the methane enters the reaction

evidence.quote: it will result that more than 25 per cent of the ~ methane enters into the reaction

props.statement: From the relative changes of methane and nitrogen (the latter inert) in the 1st example, more than 25 per cent of the methane enters into the reaction to furnish part of the liquid products, so methane can be utilized for liquid carbon compounds.

props.name: methane from the residual gas is liquefied, partially burned with oxygen and recycled

evidence.quote: The methane is separately collected and is 85 partially burned with practically pure oxy- gen

evidence.note: '20' is an OCR reading of the line number 90
evidence.quote: which produces a mixture contain- 20 ing substantially 3 volumes of hydrogen for 2 volumes of carbon monoxide, this mixture being added to the original gas mixture

props.note: partial combustion as stated in the copending application Serial No. 84,772
props.statement: After the synthesis the residual gas is expanded to liquefy its methane, which is partially burned with practically pure oxygen to give a mixture of substantially 3 volumes of hydrogen to 2 volumes of carbon monoxide that is added to the original gas mixture; hydrogen separated from the rest is also added.

props.name: no carbon deposit after several days on ethylene-rich gas

evidence.quote: Even after a continuous operation for sev- eral days, no carbon deposit is formed upon
the catalyzer nor in the reaction chamber.

props.statement: Even after continuous operation for several days on the ethylene-rich gas of the 2nd example, no carbon deposit forms on the catalyzer or in the reaction chamber.
